title: feat(mcp): a host can observe and refuse every MCP tool call through one neutral interceptor
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPMDj36ULsuXoWvUkSAxFz39)_

Part of #31605

The card stays open on merge on purpose: this branch is a project-thread branch, which no `Claim:` can name, so the PR-body claim guard would refuse a closing keyword. The landing seat finishes the card by hand.

## What changes

A host can now install one interceptor on the `mcp` service that sees every MCP tool call, on both transports, and can allow it, refuse it, or replace its result. With nothing installed, every call runs exactly as before.

- **`MCPServerRuntime.setToolInterceptor(fn)`** (plus `clearToolInterceptor`, `hasToolInterceptor`): a single slot, read at each call, so it applies to tools that registered before it was installed and to every later per-request server.
- **One seam per server, not per tool.** `routeToolCallsThrough` (new `tool-call-interceptor.ts`) wraps the server's own `registerTool` / `tool` methods right after the platform builds the server: the long-lived (stdio) server in the constructor, the per-request HTTP server in `handleHttpRequest`. Every tool registered on either server afterwards runs through it: the object, action, file and federation tools (`wireBridgeTools`), the host-injected authoring family (`registerAuthoringTools`), the bridged AI tools (`bridgeTools`), and any tool a plugin registers on `runtime.server` on `mcp:ready`, including a handler a later `RegisteredTool.update({ callback })` installs.
- **The context is server-built.** `door: 'mcp'`, `transport` (`http` | `stdio`), the registered tool name, a deep-frozen copy of the SDK-validated arguments, and a frozen principal: `userId`, `principalKind`, `onBehalfOf`, `performedBy.clientId`, `organizationId` (from `tenantId`), `environmentId`, and `isSystem: true` for a system caller. On HTTP it is projected from a new `handleHttpRequest` option, `caller: { executionContext, environmentId }`, which the runtime's `/mcp` dispatcher now fills from the request's resolved `ExecutionContext` and dispatched environment. The inbound `Request` never reaches the projection, so no header or JSON-RPC member can set a member. On stdio it is the `OS_MCP_STDIO_API_KEY` identity, resolved per call (ADR-0101); the stdio transport stamps no `environmentId`.
- **Contract.** Allow = call `next()` and return its result (or a replacement). Deny = return `{ outcome: 'deny', code, message, status? }` without calling `next()`; the client receives the coded-refusal envelope every MCP tool error uses (`isError: true`, text `{ "error": { code, message, status } }`). `outcome` is a discriminator, so a later `hold` outcome (cloud#3820 O6) can be added beside `deny` without reshaping it; today anything other than a result or a well-formed deny is refused as `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` and logged. A throw from the interceptor refuses the call (a coded throw keeps its code and status); a tool's own throw that the interceptor lets through keeps the answer it has with no interceptor. `next()` runs the tool at most once.
- **Item 5: `bridgeTools` gets the stdio principal.** Once the plugin has resolved the stdio key it binds the per-call resolver (`setRuntimeStdioPrincipal`, package-internal), and each bridged AI tool call passes `{ actor: { id, positions, permissions } }` as the registry's execution context. A runtime with no stdio principal bound still calls `execute(call)` with one argument (the existing `[#26464] stdio parity` pin is untouched and green).
- **No policy in open code.** No licence logic, no audit table, no seat rule: the same rule as the AI `ToolRegistry`'s interceptor seam.
- `@objectstack/mcp` exports the new types; `codedErrorResult` and `errorResultWithCode` are exported from `mcp-http-tools.ts` for the seam (not on the package entry).
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: the principal's `isSystem` copy is a new census read, so it gets row 66 in section 6 (reads that only carry the flag onward), and the site register is regenerated.

## Why

External AI clients reach data through the MCP tools' own bridge (`callData` on HTTP, the stdio data bridge), never through the AI `ToolRegistry`, so a host that governs in-product AI through the registry's interceptor cannot see or stop an external AI's calls. On a licensed EE, those calls never reach `sys_ai_audit_log`. This is the open-source half of cloud#3820 card 0; the cloud consumers (C1 audit row per MCP call, C2 AI seat check on the MCP door, C4 kill switch) install the interceptor after a pin.

## Verification

Tree: objectstack, this branch at the head named in the dev report (main merged at `133f75ae`).

- New `packages/mcp/src/tool-call-interceptor.test.ts`, 43 cases:
  - nothing installed: on all six paths the tool runs once and its answer equals the answer after an install-then-clear; the HTTP `caller` getters are read zero times and the stdio resolver is called zero times;
  - allow, deny and replace on each path (HTTP object tool `create_record`, HTTP action tool `list_actions`, HTTP file tool `read_file`, HTTP authoring family; stdio data tool, stdio bridged AI tool): allow serves the tool's own answer with the exact context; deny never runs the tool and answers the envelope; replace runs the tool once and serves the replacement;
  - the principal: ten spoofed identity headers and a JSON-RPC `_meta` change no member; no `caller` gives `{}`; nothing beyond the named members is projected; context, principal and arguments are frozen and the host's context is not; the stdio principal is re-resolved per call; a stdio key that fails to resolve refuses the call before the interceptor, with its code;
  - the edges: coded throw, malformed verdicts (`undefined`, `null`, a string, `{ outcome: 'hold' }`, a deny with no code, a bare object), a result seen and then not vouched for, double `next()`, a tool's own throw;
  - coverage: `registerTool`, the deprecated `tool()`, a handler installed by `update()`, and a renamed tool.
- `packages/mcp/src/__tests__/plugin-execution-context.test.ts`: a new describe starts the real plugin on stdio and pins that a bridged tool runs as the key's user and the interceptor is told that user, with the identity resolved per call.
- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.mcp.test.ts`: a new describe pins that `/mcp` passes the resolved `ExecutionContext` (by identity) and the dispatched environment as `caller`, whatever identity headers the request carries.
- Ablations (each restored from the commit): removing the HTTP routing reds 21 cases, removing the stdio routing reds 11, resolving the principal with no interceptor installed reds the two "reads nothing" pins, dropping the plugin's binding reds the plugin pin, dropping `caller` in the dispatcher reds the dispatcher pin.
- `@objectstack/mcp`: 61 files, 951 tests passed; `pnpm typecheck` (tsc + test-layer ledger) exit 0. `@objectstack/runtime`: `src/http-dispatcher.mcp*.test.ts` + `src/domains/`: 203 files, 5455 tests passed; `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. eslint on every changed file: clean.
- `dispatch-gates --commands --changed`: all 99 derived commands run locally, all exit 0, after a full `turbo run build` (120/120) for `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. `check:system-context-census` was red on the new `isSystem` read until row 66 was added. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: 14/14 current.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## Acceptance notes

- **Item 5 changes one no-interceptor behaviour, as the card asks.** On a stdio process with `OS_MCP_STDIO_API_KEY`, bridged AI tools now run with the key's user as `actor`. Before, they ran with no context, which an actor-requiring registry refuses as unauthenticated (and EE governance denies as `denied_no_actor`). A key that stops resolving now refuses the next bridged call. Nothing changes for HTTP, or for a runtime nobody bound.
- **Not a tool call, not intercepted:** stdio `resources/read` of `objectstack://objects/{object}/records/{id}` reads a record under the stdio key without a tool call, so an interceptor does not see it. The per-request HTTP server registers no resources. Whether C1 needs that read audited is the cloud card's call.
- **Cost on stdio with an interceptor installed:** the principal is resolved once more per call (for the context), beside the tool's own resolution. Zero extra reads with none installed.
- **Deny codes are relayed verbatim.** The runtime does not demote an unregistered code; a host should deny with a registered ADR-0112 code (for example `PERMISSION_DENIED`) or register its own.
- A bridged AI tool whose stdio principal fails to resolve answers the thrown message through the bridge's existing catch (no code); the interceptor path, when installed, answers the coded envelope first.
- Experimental task-based tools (`experimental.tasks.registerToolTask`) are not routed; nothing in the platform registers one. A host that calls the exported `registerObjectTools` etc. on its own `McpServer` is outside the `mcp` service's slot.
